Subject: Vendor renewals: NetSuite + Billing + Expense tool — consolidated approach

Team —

Heads up: our NetSuite maintenance expires 2027-02-28 and Chargebee (billing provider) renewal window opens in January. Procurement asked that we treat billing + expense tool renewals as a consolidated procurement to surface integration and TCO trade-offs.

I attached the RFP that Finance drafted (NetSuite_Renewal_RFP_2026.pdf). High-level asks:
- Decide whether we keep NetSuite as the system of record and renew with current bundle, or migrate billing fully to Chargebee + lightweight ERP replacement.
- Evaluate replacing Expensify (Expense tool) — Olive & Co sent a short list we can baseline against.
- Capture one consolidated SOW/contract cadence (renewal dates & cancellation windows).

Please review and respond with: 1) primary risks you see, 2) top recommendation (renew, consolidate, migrate), 3) any vendor conversations we should prioritize.

Timing: I want a recommendation memo by Dec 7 so we can include in Q1 budget planning.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Vendor renewals: NetSuite + Billing + Expense tool — consolidated approach

Jonas —

Thanks for the RFP. Quick notes after a first pass:
- NetSuite contract auto-renews unless we provide notice 60 days prior (so action needed by 2027-01-29). Contract has a termination fee clause for early exit — legal will need to quantify.
- Current annual spend on NetSuite + integrations ~ $420k (licenses + implementation support). Chargebee current spend (for hosted billing) is ~ $220k.
- Migration risk: cross-functional effort (billing, revenue ops, subscriptions team, engineering). We should budget 3–4 months of implementation effort if we move billing off NetSuite.

Recommendation (short): Run parallel procurement tracks — (A) finalize NetSuite renewal pricing & concessions if we stay, (B) ask Chargebee for a migration+discount offer and an explicit SOW. Compare total TCO over 3 years including integration & support.

I looped in Legal and Procurement (will do separately). I attached our current contract summary and the expense tool comparison we started (expense_tools_comparison_2026.xlsx).

Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks for the discussion earlier this week. Attached are two options:
1) Migration + Billing: Full migration off NetSuite billing to Chargebee. One-time migration fee + 12-month reduced platform fees. See SOW_Chargebee_2026.pdf for the migration scope.
2) Co-exist: Keep NetSuite as SoR, integrate Chargebee for subscription billing. Smaller migration effort but longer-term dual-license TCO.

Key dates: Proposal expires Jan 15, 2027 for the onboarding credit. DocuSign link for the SOW here: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/chargebee-sow-2026

Pricing summary (high level):
- Option 1: Year 1 TCO estimate $310k (including migration & discounts).
- Option 2: Year 1 incremental cost $150k (integration + Chargebee fees); NetSuite spend continues.

Happy to arrange a technical session and provide references.

Best,
